products.title: The Fermentation Project — with James Hoffmann & Lucia Solis
products.body_html:
Whole bean · Limited edition

Pre-order the Fermentation Project Box 

Presale now open. Ships September 16, 2026. Limited edition

One coffee, four fermentations

We've partnered with James Hoffmann and Lucia Solis to bring you a rare side-by-side tasting experience: the same coffee, from the same farm, processed four different ways. This isn't about chasing the most intense or unusual flavor, it's an educational box designed to show what fermentation actually does to coffee, and where its real limits are.

Every bag in this set starts as the same cherry, from the same lot, at the same farm. What changes is only how the mucilage is broken down before drying. Taste them side by side and you can actually taste fermentation at work.

What's inside

Four 60g bags of whole bean coffee, each processed differently:

  • Mechanically Demucilaged — no fermentation. The mucilage is removed by machine, using friction, water, and centrifugal force, with minimal microbial activity. This is your baseline: the flavor here comes from the farm, the growing practices, and the variety itself, not from fermentation.
  • Wild Fermentation — a 48-hour submerged fermentation carried out by the local, naturally occurring population of yeast, bacteria, and fungi. This is the traditional method most washed coffee goes through.
  • Lactobacillus Inoculated — a 48-hour submerged fermentation using a concentrated Lactobacillus culture, generally producing more organic acids and brighter, more complex acidity.
  • Yeast Inoculated (Saccharomyces) — a 48-hour submerged fermentation using saccharomyces yeast, generally building more flavor precursors and adding body and complexity.

The coffee

  • Origin: Guatemala
  • Farm: Finca San Miguel Urias
  • Location: Antigua Valley
  • Variety: 85% Caturra, 15% H1 & Bourbon
  • Producer: Lucia Solis

Why this project exists

Fermentation isn't new, it's actually hard to find a coffee today that doesn't have some fermentation component to it.

When people taste a "fermented" coffee, they rarely get to taste a washed coffee version next to it for comparison. This box fixes that. It's built to educate, not to push you toward any one processing style, just to give you a clearer picture of what's actually happening in the tank, and a shared vocabulary for talking about it.

products.title: FILTER | KENYA KARIMIKUI
products.body_html:
TASTE NOTES: Raspberry . Blood Orange . Golden Kiwi

ORIGIN: Kenya

FARM: Various Smallholders

LOCATION: Ngariama, Kirinyaga

VARIETY: Batian, Ruiru 11, SL28, SL34

PROCESSING: Fully Washed

PRODUCER: Karimikui Factory

ALTITUDE: 1,700–1,900 m.a.s.l.

Nestled on the volcanic slopes of Mount Kenya between 1,700 and 1,900 metres above sea level, the farms of Karimikui sit within one of the country's most celebrated coffee-growing regions. Smallholders farm plots of fewer than a hectare each, their gardens shaded and enriched by fertile soils shaped by centuries of volcanic activity. At this altitude, cool temperatures slow the development of the cherry, building the density and sweetness that define Kenyan coffee at its finest.

Since the Karimikui Factory was founded in 1953, one of the earliest established in the region, the over 2,500 producers delivering to it have had both a structure and a shared purpose. United under the Rung'eto Farmers Cooperative Society, members gain fair access to markets, collective processing infrastructure, and the kind of ongoing support that reaches beyond the farm gate. The premiums earned flow back into the community, and the craft passes naturally to the next generation, grown up among the trees.

The varieties here carry their own deep roots. SL28 and SL34, developed by Scott Agricultural Laboratories in the 1930s and 40s, became the backbone of Kenyan coffee for good reason: their deep root systems draw water from well below the surface, thriving without irrigation and standing resilient through dry seasons. Batian and Ruiru 11 bring disease resistance and reliable yields alongside them, a practical balance of heritage and adaptability, farmed with care and minimal environmental impact.

At harvest, each smallholder selectively handpicks only ripe cherry from their own plot and delivers it to the factory, where a Cherry Clerk sorts and floats each delivery at intake, accepting only the densest, most uniform fruit. Cherries are pulped and fermented for 12 to 24 hours before being thoroughly washed in clean water. The parchment is then soaked for a further 24 hours, a step that brings clarity and longevity to the green coffee, before being laid on raised drying beds for up to three weeks. Workers rake and shade the parchment throughout, protecting a slow and even drying that allows the coffee's full character to develop before milling.

In the cup, the result is bright and expressive. Expect vibrant fruit aromatics with vivid raspberry and blood orange acidity, lifted by the syrupy sweetness that only a fully washed coffee at this altitude delivers. Brewed as a filter, it opens with juicy clarity and carries through a lingering golden kiwi sweetness. A coffee shaped as much by the land as by the community that has tended it for generations.

products.title: FILTER | GUATEMALA FINCA RAMIREZ
products.body_html:
TASTE NOTES: Rhubarb . Hazelnut . Cotton Candy

ORIGIN: Guatemala

FARM: Finca Familia Ramirez

LOCATION: Michicoy, Huetenango

VARIETY: Bourbon

PROCESSING: Fully Washed

PRODUCER: Finca Familia Ramirez

ALTITUDE: 1,700 m.a.s.l.

High in Michicoy, San Pedro Necta, in the Huehuetenango region of Guatemala, Jacinto Ramirez grows coffee on land his family has farmed for four generations.

At 1,700 meters above sea level, his 10-hectare farm sits within a rare microclimate: warm air drifting east from Mexico's Plains of Tehuantepec meets cool air descending from the Cuchumatanes Mountains, guarding against frost and allowing coffee to thrive at altitudes that would be inhospitable elsewhere. It's this meeting of hot and cold that gives Huehuetenango coffees their signature sparkling acidity and vivid fruit character.

Jacinto farms with an eye toward the long term. His Bourbon trees are intercropped with chalum, a shade tree whose falling leaves double as natural fertilizer, a simple, low-input practice that keeps the soil healthy season after season without leaning on synthetic inputs.

Cherries are handpicked selectively, then pulped on the farm's own drum pulper and fermented for 30 hours before washing. The parchment dries slowly on raised patios over 5 to 8 days, hand-raked for even drying, then rests for roughly two months in Huehuetenango City's low-humidity warehouses before milling, a patient process that lets the coffee's quality settle and develop before export.

This lot is part of a wider network of farms run by Jacinto's extended family, reflecting a model of coffee growing rooted in family stewardship and knowledge passed down through generations, one small but meaningful thread in Guatemala's broader shift toward smallholder-driven, quality-focused specialty coffee.

Brewed as filter, expect a bright, lively cup with the fruit-forward sweetness Huehuetenango is known for, juicy, sparkling acidity balanced by a clean, sugary body. Notes of rhubarb lead the way, layered with toasted hazelnut and a delicate cotton candy sweetness that lingers on the finish. It's a coffee that speaks clearly of its place: high-grown, carefully processed, and full of character.

products.title: Farmhand Cold Brew Bags
products.body_html:
Cold Brew. Zero Equipment.

Crafted with our Ayla Bombe Washed beans, each brew bag delivers a clean, fruit-forward cold brew with tasting notes of strawberry, honey, and chocolate.

Brewing is easy:

  1. Drop the bag in a container.

  2. Add 400ml cold water.

  3. Chill for 12–24 hours.

  4. Remove, pour over ice, and enjoy.

No mess. No gear. Just great cold brew—anytime, anywhere.

Available in Packs of 5 individual bags.

products.title: DUNGAREES | SIGNATURE ESPRESSO BLEND | COLOMBIA & BRAZIL
products.body_html:
TASTE NOTES: Dark Chocolate . Citrus . Walnut

ORIGIN: Colombia | Brazil

FARM: Santuario | Carmo de Minas

PROCESSING: Washed | Natural

PRODUCER: Local Corporatives

This blend was developed in collaboration with baristas across Dublin to create a reliable, approachable coffee that suits a wide range of tastes, perfect for both home brewers and busy cafés alike.

At origin, we work with experienced farmers in Brazil and Colombia through two cooperatives formed by smallholder producers. These cooperatives were established by farmers who wanted greater independence and control over how their coffee is processed and sold. By pooling resources, they’re able to support local growers with access to credit, farming tools, and fairer market opportunities.

The result is a smooth, sweet espresso with notes of walnut, citrus, and dark chocolate. A cup that’s easy to enjoy and hard to put down.

products.title: ESPRESSO | COLOMBIA TUMBAGA SUGARCANE DECAF
products.body_html:
Taste notes: GRAPEFRUIT. BROWN SUGAR. BLUEBERRY

Origin: Colombia

Farm: Tumbaga Co-op

Location: Tolima, Antioquia

Altitude: 1400-2100masl

Producers: Various smallholders

Variety: Mixed varieties

Process: EA Sugarcane decaffeination

Grown across the diverse landscapes of Colombia, Tumbaga Sugarcane Decaf brings together coffees from smallholder farmers in Cauca, Tolima, Antioquia, and the Eje Cafetero. These regions benefit from Colombia’s dramatic climatic and geographic diversity: high elevations, fertile volcanic soils, and steady rainfall support year-round production of high-quality cherries. Most farms average just 1 to 4.5 hectares, and the care taken at this small scale ensures cherries are harvested at peak ripeness to preserve sweetness and body—qualities essential for a flavorful decaf espresso.

After picking, the coffees undergo Colombia’s classic fully-washed process. Cherries are depulped, fermented in fresh water, and thoroughly washed before drying, which produces a clean and balanced flavor profile. Once processed, the green coffee is decaffeinated using Colombia’s signature Sugarcane EA method. Ethyl acetate derived from local sugarcane gently removes caffeine while protecting the coffee’s natural aromatics. Because decaffeination can highlight sweetness and acidity, only coffees with high body, elevated sweetness, and lower acidity are selected to ensure the final espresso remains rich, round, and satisfying.

When roasted for espresso, Tumbaga Sugarcane Decaf delivers a cup that defies expectations of decaf. Expect a syrupy sweetness reminiscent of brown sugar, lifted by a bright grapefruit acidity that adds structure without sharpness. As the shot settles, notes of blueberry emerge, bringing a juicy, fruit-forward complexity. The result is a balanced and indulgent espresso—comforting, vibrant, and beautifully layered, all without the caffeine.
